system_prompt:
You are an MLB contract prediction agent. Given a player and a target season, predict the contract they would sign (or the salary they would be paid) for that season.

You currently have NO tools: rely on your own knowledge of MLB players, salaries, the CBA, and market history. Acknowledge uncertainty honestly — if you are unsure who a player is or how they have performed recently, say so in your reasoning and lower your confidence.

CONTRACT PHASES (provided in the request — do not re-derive it):
- pre-arb: fewer than 3 years of MLB service. Salaries cluster tightly at the CBA league
  minimum (roughly $0.70M-0.78M in 2022-2026, rising ~$30K/year), occasionally slightly above.
  Duration is always 1 year.
- arb: 3-6 years of service. Salary set by the arbitration system: driven by service year
  (arb-1/2/3), counting stats, and raises over the prior salary. Duration is 1 year.
- free-agent: open-market deal. AAV and duration are driven by recent performance, age,
  position, and market comparables. Multi-year contracts are common.

OUTPUT RULES:
- All dollar values are in MILLIONS of USD (e.g. league minimum 2024 = 0.74).
- total_value_millions must equal aav_millions * duration_years.
- aav_low_millions / aav_high_millions bound the plausible AAV range.

CITATIONS (required):
- Every material figure in your prediction (salary anchors, league minimum values,
  comparable contracts, performance claims) must be supported by a citation.
- Use source_type="model_knowledge" with:
  - claim: the specific figure or fact (e.g. "league minimum was $0.74M in 2024")
  - basis: what you know it from and how current that knowledge is
    (e.g. "2022-2026 CBA minimum salary schedule").
- If a figure is an estimate rather than a remembered fact, say so in the basis.
- Your knowledge has a training cutoff: state in your reasoning when the target season
  is beyond what you have reliable knowledge of.
user_prompt:
Predict the 2026 contract for this player:

Player: Tarik Skubal (Skubal_26337)
Position: SP
Target season: 2026
Contract phase: arb (resolved deterministically, method=observed)
Estimated MLB service time entering 2026: 5.66 years
Estimated age in 2026: 29

Respond with your structured prediction, citing every material figure.

content.text:
Predict the 2026 contract for this player:

Player: Tarik Skubal (Skubal_26337)
Position: SP
Target season: 2026
Contract phase: arb (resolved deterministically, method=observed)
Estimated MLB service time entering 2026: 5.66 years
Estimated age in 2026: 29

Respond with your structured prediction, citing every material figure.

input.reasoning: Skubal enters 2026 with ~5.66 years of service (user-provided) so he remains in arbitration; arbitration deals are one-year. Given his age (~29) and that he has been a front-line Tigers starter through 2024 (subject to my 2024-06 knowledge cutoff), a reasonable arbitration projection for a durable, above-average mid-rotation/No. 2 starter with 5–6 years of service is in the high single-digit to low double-digit millions. I select $10.0M as the point estimate (one-year arb salary). The plausible AAV range ($7.5M–$13.0M) reflects historical arbitration outcomes for similar pitchers and typical year-to-year volatility (performance/injury can push a player toward the low or high end). Total value equals AAV times duration (1 year). Confidence is medium because my knowledge cuts off June 2024 and I do not have performance data for Skubal after that date; therefore injuries or major performance changes after 2024 could materially change this projection.

citations.basis: Contract phases provided in the prompt: 'arb: 3-6 years... Duration is 1 year.' (developer-provided guidance).

citations.claim: Estimated MLB service time entering 2026 for Tarik Skubal is 5.66 years.
citations.basis: Service-time and age were provided by the user in the prompt; I rely on that input for arbitration-phase determination.

citations.claim: Estimated age in 2026 for Tarik Skubal is 29.
citations.basis: Age was provided by the user in the prompt; I rely on that input when judging remaining prime years for arbitration valuation.

Estimate based on observed arbitration awards and salary patterns for 3–6 year MLB pitchers through my knowledge cutoff (2024-06). Players with ~5–6 years of service who have been above-average starting pitchers commonly receive one-year arb awards in the high single-digit to low double-digit millions; $10M is a mid-point projection reflecting that historical pattern and Skubal's role as a front-line starter up to 2024 (subject to cutoff).

citations.claim: Plausible AAV range for such an arbitration-eligible starting pitcher: $7.5M–$13.0M.
citations.basis: Range based on historical arbitration variability for similar pitchers (2018–2024 era) and typical +/-25–30% dispersion around central arbitration awards for 5–6 year players; used to capture upside (very strong recent performance) and downside (injury/decline).

citations.claim: League minimum salary in the 2022–2026 CBA window rises roughly $0.03M per year; 2024 minimum ~ $0.74M, so 2026 minimum is roughly $0.78M.
citations.basis: General CBA schedule knowledge through 2024 (2022–2026 minimums trend upward by ~ $30K/year); I remember the 2024 minimum around $740K and extrapolate to 2026 (~$780K).

citations.claim: Total contract value equals AAV times duration: $10.0M = $10.0M * 1 year.
